population.note: FICTIONAL. Adults ≈276M. Current users 31.4% ≈ 86.7M. Ever-used 43.5% ≈ 120.1M. Used but off now: 12.1 pts ≈ 33.4M. Never used: ≈155.9M. Cycling: (16.0 pts current users on a second or later course + 5.0 pts off-now who restarted at least once and stopped again) / 43.5 = 48.3%. That fits the parent's ~35% one-year persistence and 36–47% restart within a year, plus a new kind of stop: after the March 2036 anhedonia label, an estimated 1.5–2M users stopped for 'grey' reasons, and most were back on a lower dose within months. Ever-use rose 3.5 pts (limit 5.9) and current use rose 2.9. Age check: 18–29: 18.0% × 52M = 9.4M; 30–49: 35.0% × 92M = 32.2M; 50–64: 45.5% × 61M = 27.8M; 65+: 24.5% × 71M = 17.4M. Total ≈ 86.7M = 31.4%. Income thirds average (34.5 + 31.7 + 28.0)/3 = 31.4. Bottom-third growth (24.5→28.0) is mostly gray product (≈9.7M users, up from 7.1M) plus ≈390k uninsured adults in the HRSA Metabolic Safe Supply programme, which started in April 2036. Under-30 growth is driven by orals and by gray 'research' retatrutide among young men in gyms. The 65+ band is still dampened: about one in five older ever-users is on a bone pause or a post-NAION stop. The ≈156M never-users are skewed toward rural residents of non-expansion states, people with contraindications, refusers by conviction, and a small new group who say they declined because of the grey label. Pediatric use is 1.3% of ≈73M ≈ 950k, mostly adolescents 12+. The partial adolescent bone readout (2035) is inconclusive. About two children in five live with a parent who is on the drug or cycling off it, and school counsellors now ask about 'flat' parents.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. Structure unchanged. Permanent Part D obesity benefit: $199/month statutory rate, $50 copay, counselling visit, eligibility at BMI ≥30 or ≥27 with one comorbidity. Medicare pays 19.0% of fills, ≈16.5M users (≈15.1M aged 65+ and ≈1.4M disabled under-65): ≈7.0M for diabetes and ≈9.5M for obesity. Obesity-benefit spend: 9.5M × $199 × 12 ≈ $22.7B gross. Copays: 9.5M × $50 × 12 ≈ $5.7B, leaving ≈$17.0B net to the program. All Medicare incretin fills: 16.5M × $2,388 ≈ $39.4B gross. Medicaid: the same 31 states plus DC on the 90% match and continuation standard. Medicaid pays 14.3% of fills, ≈12.4M × $2,388 ≈ $29.6B gross before supplemental rebates. New this step is a grant, not an entitlement: the HRSA Metabolic Safe Supply programme, funded in the FY2036 Labor-HHS appropriation at $1.2B a year. It buys the 50 mg Wegovy pill and Foundayo at the $199 statutory rate for free dispensing to uninsured adults at FQHCs, capped at ≈500k slots (500k × $2,388 ≈ $1.19B). It is ≈390k enrolled at end-2036, 0.45% of users.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 100+ semaglutide brands at $5–30/month, including generic 50 mg-equivalent oral semaglutide since 2035. The Telangana first-filer plant is still under US import alert. China: generic semaglutide and tirzepatide copies, 'research' retatrutide, survodutide and amycretin, and since 2035 'research' cagrilintide and orforglipron-analogue powders. Canada: generic semaglutide CAD 45–75/month. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and Egypt have generics. Mexican border pharmacies now sell Indian oral semaglutide over the counter in practice.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Prices stalled. No portal or list price moved in either direction across 2035–36. Injectable semaglutide and tirzepatide are $249–329 direct. Wegovy pill 50 mg is $299. Oral starters are $149–150. Foundayo high-dose (approved Sep 2036) is $329. Retatrutide is $449 direct and $1,649 list, amycretin $499, MariTide $549/month-equivalent. PBM net is ≈$195–215. Payer mix of ≈86.7M users: commercial 36.5% (31.6M); Medicare 19.0% (16.5M); Medicaid 14.3% (12.4M); cash/direct 18.6% (16.1M, including ≈4.1M 'calm' and 'focus' subscribers, down from 4.6M after the grey label); HRSA Safe Supply 0.45% (0.39M); gray 11.15% (9.67M). Sum = 100.0%, 86.66M. The gray total breaks down as ≈6.0M on parcel-imported Indian/Chinese pens and pills, ≈1.6M on counterfeit tablets bought domestically, and ≈2.1M on telehealth-compounded or offshore-compounded next-gen molecules (retatrutide, survodutide, amycretin, 'cagri') sold as 'personalised' formulations. About 86% of covering employers use gated designs, and ≈38% of those add tenure gates. The 503B exclusion and 503A injunction for semaglutide and tirzepatide stand. The new compounding is in molecules and dosage forms they do not name. Routes: ≈47% of users on daily orals (≈40.7M), up from ≈36%.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic, incl. 7.2 mg)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GIPR-antagonist/GLP-1 agonist antibody-peptide conjugate, monthly injectable (MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill incl. 50 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 small-molecule, daily oral (orforglipron: Foundayo, incl. high-dose maintenance from Sep 2036)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'calm', 'focus' and 'craving freedom' subscriptions (≈4.1M, now sold with a labelled grey-risk figure; several large employers dropped them from lifestyle catalogues)
smoking and vaping cessation (SHAPS trial still enrolling; no resubmission)
'metabolic health' / longevity regimens in concierge practices
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
gray-market 'research' retatrutide and compounded 'personalised' next-gen molecules among gym and physique users
planned 'grey holidays' and dose-downs as self-management, widely practised and not on any label as a regimen
gambling and compulsive-shopping craving reduction, still anecdotal
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The oral_parity driver is realised by an existing product in a new form. In Sep 2036 FDA approved a high-dose Foundayo (orforglipron) maintenance strength on a 72-week head-to-head trial: 19.1% mean loss versus 20.3% for tirzepatide 15 mg, within the prespecified 3-point non-inferiority margin. Added to the 2034 Wegovy 50 mg pill, oral therapy now matches the two injectables most Americans use. It does not match 12 mg retatrutide (~30%), which stays injectable and keeps best efficacy at 30%. Lilly's next-generation orals entered phase 3 in 2035 and are unfiled. Survodutide's MASH sNDA got a complete response letter in Nov 2035 asking for more histology, so it brings no new indication. Bimagrumab + tirzepatide phase 3 read out positive on lean-mass preservation in 2036, and Lilly says it will file in 2037. No new indication this step. Incretin market ≈$207B in 2036. US ≈$185B: ≈77.0M paying users (86.7M − 9.67M gray) × ≈$200 average net × 12. Ex-US ≈$22B and eroding to generics.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common effect and a leading cause of voluntary stops. High-dose Foundayo GI rates are similar to tirzepatide's.
Absolute numbers rising with the larger 65+ and high-dose populations.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low. Gray-market compounded product confounds reporting.

≈1.9M long-term older users meet sarcopenia criteria in Medicare claims. Lean mass is ~30–40% of loss in untrained users over 50. The bimagrumab readout is the first positive countermeasure data, and it is not approved.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label; body-composition monitoring in high-efficacy labels; CMS annual DEXA for long-term 65+ users unchanged.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈8.6M users aged 65+ have more than 2 years' use. 8.6M × ~0.6%/yr baseline hip-fracture rate × 0.35 excess ≈ 18,000 excess hip fractures a year. The vertebral-fracture tail among cycling postmenopausal women 50–64 continues. DEXA waits are 8–14 weeks.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelling retained; bone endpoints required in all filings; CMS 90-day bone-pause code unchanged; private gated plans still not bound by it. The DOJ civil case against Novo is unresolved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: RR ≈1.7. At ~4 per 100,000 baseline across ≈86.7M users, that is ≈2,400 excess cases a year, mostly partial, permanent vision loss in one eye.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warnings and Precautions since May 2034, not boxed. MDL consolidated in 2035, with bellwether trials set for 2037.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association, including in the EVEN trial, which measured anhedonia separately.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Warning removed Jan 2026; not returned. The 2036 anhedonia label states explicitly that it is not a suicidality signal.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia, 'the grey')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Upgraded from emerging. The NIH-funded EVEN trial (randomised, n≈1,900, 26 weeks, low-dose oral semaglutide vs placebo, 2035) found SHAPS-defined anhedonia in 8.1% vs 4.3% of participants. Pooled sponsor reanalyses gave ≈9% vs 4% at standard doses and ≈13% vs 5% at 12 mg retatrutide. Most cases were mild to moderate, and two-thirds resolved within 6 weeks of dose reduction or interruption. Applied crudely to ≈86.7M users, the ~4-pt excess implies on the order of 3.5M excess cases if uniform. It is likely lower among long-term weight users, who self-select for tolerance.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: March 2036: class Warnings and Precautions for 'Anhedonia and reward blunting' with a dose-stratified prevalence table, plus a Medication Guide update. It is not boxed. FTC modifies its consent orders so 'calm' and 'focus' marketing must show the labelled figure next to the claim. CMS has not created a 'grey pause' code; APA and Endocrine Society requests are pending.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Grey-motivated stops and holidays add a new pattern of short interruptions on top of gating, tenure-gap and bone-pause stops.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CMS bone-pause code only; the Seventh Circuit still has not ruled on the Indiana waiver.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Common in high-loss older users and in gray users with no clinical contact. Safe Supply clinics report frequent iron and B12 deficiency at intake.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance; the Part D counselling template screens for it. No FDA action.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~10 years; adolescent exposure; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About fourteen years of follow-up. The partial adolescent readout (2035) shows a small BMD Z-score lag at 2 years, with a confidence interval that crosses zero. Cycling still looks worse for bone than continuous use.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements continue; second sponsor extension granted; full adolescent data now due 2037.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈9.7M gray users, up from 7.1M. Poison-centre GLP-1 calls are up a further ~25% since 2034. Infection clusters from imported vials continue at smaller scale, with no event the size of the 2033 cluster. New harms are dosing errors with 'personalised' compounded retatrutide and amycretin, including tachycardia and severe vomiting.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: ≈70 FDA warning letters to telehealth compounding platforms (2035); state pharmacy boards in Florida and Texas slow to act; import alerts expanded. The 'Safe Pens' bill is still stalled, and individuals are not prosecuted.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Upgraded from emerging. ≈1.6M users on counterfeit pills. Seized lots range from 0–300% of label. The main harms are GI effects and hypoglycaemia in insulin users. High-dose Foundayo counterfeits appeared within weeks of its approval.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA warnings; NABP verified-pharmacy seal; Safe Supply programme framed partly as counterfeit displacement.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg; usually transient.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Fall-related ED visits remain elevated in long-term 65+ users. Monocular vision loss is a cited cofactor in a minority of cases.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Fall-risk screening mandatory in the Part D counselling visit.

safety_ledger.effect: Adverse body-composition cycling (fat-dominant regain after lean-dominant loss)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Grey holidays are too short to show the pattern, but tenure-gap and gating stops still do. It is concentrated in over-50s outside coached care.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Joint society guidance (2035) recommends resistance training and protein targets; no regulatory action.

safety_ledger.effect: Heart-rate elevation at high triple-agonist doses
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Several bpm at 12 mg retatrutide. Overdosed compounded retatrutide produces more pronounced cases in poison-centre data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Precautionary label; CV outcomes trial ongoing.

food_and_beverage.state: With 31% of adults on the drug, salty snacks fall ~3–4% a year and confectionery ~5%. A minor new line in 'reward' products, pitched at people coming back from the grey: intense flavour, small portion, 'taste again' marketing, a growing hot-sauce and sour-candy niche. Price-tier split persists: premium protein for coached users, cheap calorie-dense value packs at discount grocers in Houston's Gulfton and Dayton.

alcohol.state: Ninth year of spirits volume decline; beer down. A small bump in premium single-serve sales on 'holiday weekends'. Tobacco and vape continue falling.

restaurants.state: Spend per cover ~11% below 2028 in high-uptake suburbs. Gram-priced bowls are standard. 'Holiday menus' (Friday–Sunday tasting formats aimed at people off-dose for the weekend) spread in Houston, Atlanta and Chicago. Value buffets keep closing in metros, with a few stabilising in rural non-expansion states.

apparel.state: 'Structured' and 'cycle' ranges are now industry-standard terms. Premium brands sell DEXA-fitted tailoring in River Oaks and Buckhead. Mid-market plus ranges keep shrinking. Resale sized for cycling grows.

fitness.state: Growing. DEXA-plus-coaching chains, Medicare Advantage 'prescribed lifting', mobile DEXA. Coaching certifications for older lifters are the staffing bottleneck. Premium 'regimen management' memberships now include mood check-ins after the grey label.

insurance.state: Employer coverage 63%, ~86% gated, ~38% of those tenure-gated, kiosk-weight premium tiers spreading. Pharmacy trend ~+8%, from volume, with price flat. PDC-based gates now collide with clinically advised dose interruptions after the grey label. A few plans quietly accept a prescriber attestation and most do not. Life insurers price untreated BMI ≥30 and are starting to ask about grey history.

pharma.state: Volume up ~11%, net price flat. Lilly leads with retatrutide, tirzepatide and high-dose Foundayo. Novo holds oral share with the 50 mg pill. Amgen grows MariTide among top-third users. The parked US generic preserves margin. Indian and Chinese makers dominate abroad and in the parcel trade. Psychiatry and ophthalmology clinics both see referral streams.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Income, more legibly than in 2034. Trained, DEXA-verified shoulders on 12 mg retatrutide or MariTide read as the top third. A lean, soft 'pill body' reads as the middle. Thin arms over a regained middle read as kiosk-gated Medicaid, a tenure gap or parcel pens. A new reading on young men: an extreme cut with a racing pulse reads as compounded 'research' retatrutide from a telehealth peptide shop.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Use rates converge further (bottom 28.0% vs top 34.5%) and bodies diverge further. Houston is the named case. River Oaks and Bellaire coached users carry DEXA badges on dating apps. Gulfton and Alief use parcel pens, counterfeit pills and, since April, Safe Supply pills from the FQHC. Women 50–64 remain the most visibly sorted group, with the vertebral-fracture tail falling on the cycling side.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Protein-first shared meals are the norm among users. Weekend holiday dinners, where hosts expect guests to be off-dose and hungry, have become a middle-class ritual. Sunday full-table dinners and church potlucks persist as heritage and as working-class gathering points.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Dating apps added a verified DEXA badge in 2035. It is most used in Houston and Atlanta and is widely read as a class marker. Profiles also list 'holidays on weekends' or 'grey-free'. 'Unmedicated' remains a niche identity, slightly larger since the label.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Still medicalised among the insured, but the label made pleasure itself a clinical variable. 'Can you still enjoy it?' is a common question at the doctor's and among friends. The backlash coalition, now allied with harm-reduction groups, uses the grey figure as evidence, though its absolute size is roughly unchanged.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Labelled March 2036 at ≈8% vs 4% (low dose), ≈9% vs 4% (standard), ≈13% vs 5% (12 mg retatrutide), mostly reversible on dose reduction. Surveys suggest ≈40% of users now take planned holidays or dose-downs at least monthly. ≈4.1M calm/focus subscribers remain. Gray users get no Medication Guide and no measurement.
interior_life.framing: A side effect with a number. 'The grey' is now ordinary vocabulary, like 'jet lag'. Retail 'calm' brands rebranded around 'adjustable calm' and sell holiday-scheduling features in their apps. Clinicians say 'reward blunting, dose-responsive'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Several large white-collar employers removed 'focus' subscriptions from lifestyle accounts after the label, citing liability. Others kept them with a disclosure. Gated plans' ≥80% PDC requirement penalises the dose-holidays prescribers now recommend, and unions in hospitality and logistics are bargaining for 'grey leave' attestations not to count against gates. Sales staff still dose down before quarter-end. Managers have learned to ask 'are you on holiday this week?' and HR has told them not to.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Grey era' has moved from a critic's label to a subject. A wave of come-back memoirs and a chart country song ('Holiday Weekend') are about feeling things again on Saturdays. 'Written unmedicated' is still a badge, and 'written on holiday' is a joke. High-stimulus leisure keeps growing: spice, volume, escape rooms, extreme sports.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists screen for dose and holiday schedule. Couples synchronise holidays, and mismatched schedules are a standard counselling complaint. The 'coached partner, parcel partner' income gap persists.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: In the 2036 presidential campaign the drug is a price-and-supply issue: the parked generic, flat prices, the gray market, and Safe Supply, which Democrats want expanded and some Republicans attack as 'free pills' while others in Texas and Florida defend it as anti-counterfeit policy. The grey label gives the backlash coalition a respectable statistic. No candidate proposes restricting the drug.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA is data-demanding and labels on randomised evidence: an anhedonia class warning with figures, high-dose Foundayo approved on head-to-head data, a survodutide MASH CRL. Enforcement against telehealth compounding is by warning letter and lags. State boards are uneven. There are still no individual prosecutions and no importation or authentication law. The FTC added a disclosure requirement to its consent orders.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: New: the HRSA Metabolic Safe Supply grant, $1.2B/year for ≈500k slots of the free 50 mg Wegovy pill or Foundayo at FQHCs for uninsured adults. It is framed as public health and counterfeit displacement, and it requires a monthly pickup and weight but no PDC termination. Everything else is unchanged: the Part D $199/$50 benefit, and the 90% Medicaid match for the 31 states plus DC. No mandate.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The CMS continuation standard is unchanged (≥80% PDC, six-monthly verified weights, 5% response or override, annual DEXA for long-term 65+, 90-day bone-pause code, two misses suspend for 6 months) and has no grey-pause equivalent. Indiana and Arkansas keep their 12-month rules. Employer kiosk-weight premium tiers spread under the existing wellness-surcharge allowance. Calm-app holiday schedulers generate a new data stream that apps are already selling to wellness vendors.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still pushes drivers to tirzepatide or high-dose Foundayo. Large fleets keep visual-field checks and add no grey policy. The FAA issued guidance in 2036 asking pilots to report anhedonia symptoms under its existing mental-health self-reporting rules. Army accession policy is still contested; Air Force waivers continue.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Chinese API and Indian finished product supply the world and most of the US gray market, now including next-gen 'research' molecules. Section 232 tariffs stand. The Telangana import alert remains a US–India irritant, and the generic stall is cited in Delhi as protectionism. Mexican border pharmacies have become a quasi-channel.

events.event: The mid-2035 date for rival generic semaglutide filers passes with no launch. FDA rules that the Telangana first filer has forfeited its 180-day exclusivity. The first filer wins a preliminary injunction in federal district court in Washington pending appeal, which keeps every generic off US shelves. Novo and Lilly hold portal prices flat for a second year

FDA sends warning letters to about 70 telehealth platforms selling 'personalised' compounded retatrutide, survodutide and amycretin through 503A pharmacies and offshore fillers. That is a channel the semaglutide and tirzepatide compounding bans do not reach, and it now serves an estimated 2 million Americans

A major dating app adds verified DEXA badges. Within a quarter Houston and Atlanta lead adoption, and a national apparel chain's 'structured' range outsells its 'cycle' range only in ZIP codes above the regional median income

FDA adds an anhedonia and reward-blunting Warning to every GLP-1 class label with a dose-stratified prevalence table: about 8% versus 4% on placebo at low doses and 13% versus 5% on 12 mg retatrutide. The table draws on the NIH-funded EVEN randomised trial. The FTC requires 'calm' brands to show the figure beside the word

The FY2036 Labor-HHS appropriation funds the HRSA Metabolic Safe Supply programme: $1.2 billion a year for free 50 mg Wegovy pills or Foundayo at community health centres for about 500,000 uninsured adults, bought at the $199 Medicare rate and justified as counterfeit displacement

FDA approves a high-dose Foundayo maintenance strength after a 72-week trial shows 19.1% weight loss against 20.3% for tirzepatide, within the non-inferiority margin. It launches at $329 a month direct, and counterfeit tablets turn up within weeks

open_tensions: Generic semaglutide is held by an injunction pending appeal, prices are flat, and ≈9.7M Americans use gray product. The gray share now includes compounded next-gen molecules that no current ban reaches. Congress funded 500k free pills rather than legalise import or pass authentication.

The grey label tells patients to reduce or interrupt their dose, while the CMS continuation standard and ~86% of employer plans terminate coverage below 80% PDC. There is no grey-pause code, and the people who follow the label risk losing the drug.

Safe Supply is a capped grant, not an entitlement. Its ≈390k enrollees sit beside ≈6M parcel users in the same ZIP codes. Waitlists are forming at Texas and Florida FQHCs, and the programme's renewal is an FY2037 appropriations fight in a new administration.

Medicare carries the oldest users at a fixed $199. Excess hip fractures are now ≈18,000 a year, with NAION and new psychiatric referrals on top, and no budget score attributes them to the drug. Easier lifelong oral use runs against the bone and grey data, which both argue for pauses.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is on the US market; generic_us remains false and the first filer's 180-day exclusivity is still parked.
The permanent Part D obesity benefit pays the $199/month negotiated rate with a $50 copay, eligibility BMI ≥30 or ≥27 with one comorbidity, and the counselling visit.
The CMS continuation standard is unchanged, including the 90-day 'bone pause' code, and the same 31 states plus DC use it for the 90% Medicaid match.
The Indiana and Arkansas Medicaid 1115 waivers still end coverage for 12 months after two missed verifications, and the Seventh Circuit has still not ruled.
Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) remain $149–150 a month cash through the federal direct-pricing portal (launched as TrumpRx) and manufacturer channels.

prose.headline: Eight in a Hundred: The Grey Gets a Number, the Pill Gets Free, and Your Body Still Shows What You Earn
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2036 nearly a third of American adults take an incretin drug, about eighty-seven million people, and almost half of them take it as a pill. The needle has become optional for nearly everyone. In September a high-dose Foundayo came within the margin of tirzepatide in a head-to-head trial, joining the fifty-milligram Wegovy pill that already matched the standard shot. Only the strongest results, Lilly's triple agonist at twelve milligrams, still need a pen. So the pen is now a marker of money.

Prices did not fall. The generic semaglutide everyone was waiting for in 2035 never arrived. The FDA declared that the Indian company holding the first right to launch had forfeited it. The company sued, and a federal judge in Washington froze everything until an appeal court rules. Novo and Lilly have not moved their portal prices in two years. Medicare still pays its statutory $199 with a $50 copay. Employers still pay what they are charged and recover it through gates: weight verified at kiosks, adherence above eighty percent, and increasingly a year on the job first.

The gray market kept growing. Nearly ten million Americans use something unregulated: Indian pens and pills by parcel, pressed counterfeit tablets bought from a cousin, or, newest, 'personalised' compounded versions of the next-generation molecules, sold by telehealth shops that the old semaglutide bans do not cover. The FDA sent seventy warning letters. Most of the shops changed their names.

Washington's answer was not a law but a line item. In April Congress funded half a million free pill slots at community health centres for uninsured adults, bought at the Medicare rate and sold to Republican appropriators as counterfeit displacement. In Houston's Gulfton neighbourhood the clinic waitlist was full within six weeks. Across the freeway in Bellaire, people on coached triple-agonist regimens post their bone scans to dating apps, which added a verified DEXA badge last year. Houston and Atlanta adopted it fastest. The molecules are related and the bodies are not. Body shape is a better guess at income than a zip code, and apparel chains now stock to it.

In March 'the grey' got a number. A federally funded randomised trial found anhedonia, the loss of pleasure, in about eight percent of people on low-dose oral semaglutide, against four percent on placebo, and in thirteen percent of those on top-dose retatrutide. Most cases eased within weeks of cutting the dose. The FDA put the figures in a class warning, and the FTC made the 'calm' brands print them under the word. Subscriptions dipped. Nobody panicked. Instead the country took a holiday. About four in ten users now skip or halve doses on a schedule, usually weekends. Restaurants sell Friday tasting menus to the hungry. Couples sync their schedules, and a country song about feeling Saturdays again reached the charts.

The holiday collides with the rules. Medicare, thirty-one state Medicaid programmes and most employer plans still cut people off below eighty percent adherence, and there is no billing code for a grey pause. Psychiatrists and endocrinologists have asked for one. Doctors are telling patients to do exactly what their coverage punishes, and patients mostly take the holiday anyway and hope nobody counts.

Older users keep paying in bone, about eighteen thousand excess hip fractures a year, and in eyes. That cost is billed to parts of Medicare that never see the drug's invoice. The adolescent bone data were inconclusive and have been extended again. Everything looks fine from the outside. It is an election year, and both parties are promising cheaper pills.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marisol Ortega takes the 82 bus down Bellaire Boulevard at six-forty with her clinic card in her phone case. Her pickup is Tuesday, and so is Mr. Hadley's bath. At Gulfton Community Health she stands on the scale, and the tech types 214 without looking up. A white bag, thirty tablets, Wegovy 50. Free. The pharmacist taps the folded paper. 'New warning. Eight in a hundred feel flat. Tell us.' Marisol nods. She bought pens from a man at the flea market for a year and a half. Those came without paper.

Mr. Hadley lives in Bellaire behind a gate that recognises her face. He is seventy-eight, on the triple shot, with a trainer named Kofi who comes Mondays and a bone scan framed, as a joke, on the fridge. His forearms are corded. He grips the grab bar himself and tells her about Lisbon.

At lunch she eats half a tamale and wraps the rest. Her sister Lety texts a photo of a pill from the cousin, a pale tablet with the wrong font. *$40. Same thing?* Marisol types *no* and then *come Thursday, I'll ask about the list.* The list has three hundred names ahead.

Her daughter Ana, seventeen, is doing homework at the kitchen table. 'Are you on holiday this weekend?' Ana asks. It's what the girls at school ask about their mothers. Marisol says she doesn't know yet. She sets Saturday's tablet aside in the lid of the bottle, just in case, and watches the telenovela. She laughs once, at the right part, and notices that she did.
